We expect to fund potential acquisitions through a combination of debt financing (which may include borrowings under our existing or new credit facilities, term loans or other debt instruments), seller financing, the issuance of our common stock or other equity or equity-linked securities, including equity interests in our subsidiaries.

The decline in gross margin from the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 was primarily due to a shift in sales mix toward our larger distribution and key account partners, with this shift expected to continue through the fourth quarter.
During December 2025, the Company committed to a plan to dispose of its Inpixon Business and initiated a process to identify a buyer.

Additionally, as of September 30, 2026, the Company’s obligations include $4.7 million of debt (See Note 8 – Debt), operating lease liabilities of approximately $1.4 million, including approximately $0.6 million that is expected to be paid in the next twelve months, and $5.9 million drawn on its credit facility, which matures on February 11, 2029.
The Company also expects to recognize cost savings from the wind down of the TriFan 600 and ADS development programs.

Management’s plans to address these capital requirements include implementing cost optimization measures, including the wind-down of the ADS division; renegotiating vendor contract terms; and pursuing additional debt or equity financing.
There can be no assurance that these plans will be successfully implemented or that they will alleviate the substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern.
These amounts exclude prefunded warrants and warrants that management does not expect to be redeemed due to the exercise price.

dropped.t: (Nasdaq: XTIA) (“XTI Aerospace,” “XTI” or the “Company”), an aerospace and advanced technology platform and parent company of Drone Nerds, LLC (“Drone Nerds”), a leading drone solutions platform serving commercial, enterprise and government customers, today announced that its internal review, initiated in July 2026, has been completed and the Company is on track to file its Form 10-Q by October 26, 2026.

“With the internal review complete, I am happy to report that there were no financial misstatements discovered and we are on track to report our second quarter results later this month,” said Jeremy Schneiderman, Interim CEO.

Consistent with its ongoing commitment to strong corporate governance, the Company intends to implement, under the oversight of the Board of Directors, certain enhancements to its governance framework, policies and procedures.
The Board will continue to evaluate the Company’s governance practices and may adopt additional measures as it deems appropriate.
The Company anticipates reporting second quarter revenue of approximately $32.4 million, gross profit of approximately $5.6 million and loss from operations of approximately $9.1 million.
The Company is withdrawing its previously issued 2026 financial guidance at this time and expects to provide a comprehensive update at a later date.
